low_level: Registers 40 to 255 over the 217 distinct kernels behind the card's cells (24 with register spills, a kernel measured in more than one batch counts once), shared memory 672 to 22528 bytes, harness 0.10 on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99.
Adapter statics: input arrangement striped, output indices, temp storage 640 to 2304 bytes.
Oracle battery (23 cases per cell plus the measurement seeds) passed on every cell that has a number, 49 cells unsupported by the adapter's contract or the device, no cell failed the oracle.
algorithmic: Random input (the one-node matrix on gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): latency not_guaranteed wins 21 of 60 cells (runner-up in 23), latency prefer_smaller_index wins 20 of 50 cells (runner-up in 17), throughput not_guaranteed wins 34 of 59 cells (runner-up in 8), throughput prefer_smaller_index wins 30 of 50 cells (runner-up in 6).

Where it wins on random input (bf16 N 512, bf16 N 1024, bf16 N 2048, bf16 N 4096, fp32 N 512, fp32 N 1024, fp32 N 2048, fp32 N 4096), the median margin over the runner-up is +47 percent and over the scope's reference control +941 percent.

Largest random-input deficits (distinct cells, worst regime): fp32 N 256 k 64 +216 percent behind N6w_atom32 in latency not_guaranteed, bf16 N 256 k 64 +185 percent behind N5_rows_f in throughput not_guaranteed, fp32 N 256 k 48 +141 percent behind N6w_atom32 in latency prefer_smaller_index, bf16 N 256 k 48 +129 percent behind N5_rows_f in throughput not_guaranteed.
Named workloads won on random input: moe_nemotron3_ultra_512_top22, nsa_blocks_128k, nsa_blocks_32k, peer_subkey_top16.
negative: The GB200 pass measured random input only on one host (gb200-nvl4-ts2-99): the tie_heavy, shuffled-tie and phase 3b order-check findings for this adapter are on its B200 card.

The fp32 sorted-finish defect found by the B200 phase 3b order check (equal keys inside the top k left in scatter order under prefer_smaller_index, k 16 and 64 at N 512, 2048 and 4096) is a property of the same code and stands for this card, the GB200 pass measured unsorted output only.
surprises: None beyond what the tables show.
open_questions: The fix is the tie rewrite generalized to every class run inside the top k, open is whether the sorted output then costs anything over the unsorted path.

B200 pass (WINNERS_b200.md, random input on umbriel-b200-047, tie_heavy on 068, shuffled ties on 094, phase 3b on 047): the warp and sub-warp winners agree with GB200 on 359 of 376 common cells (365 of 376 when each cell is compared through the adapters both passes measured, as section 16 of the knowledge base does), the differences are named sub-warp lane-count cells, N 128 sub-warp throughput cells and warp ties within 5 percent, and in the block matrices the B1_idx against B1_det2 throughput ties fall either way. On GB200 the k 64 cells at 128 threads run 3 to 15 percent slower than on B200 (hw-researcher, a generation property) and the aarch64 cicc emits branches for the conditional swaps (T20, 3 to 4 percent).
